item.title: Iran says U.S. military not allowed in Gulf "under any circumstance"
item.description: The U.S. ambassador to the U.N. says the war with Iran could last another year, but he hopes Tehran will "come to the table" sooner.

item.title: Kim Jon-un visits China to open new bridge, reaffirm ties
item.description: The North Korean leader used the trip to reaffirm ties with its powerful neighbor.

item.title: "48 Hours" show schedule
item.description: "48 Hours" uncovers the narrative behind true crime cases with unmatched reporting and suspense.

item.title: Man's murder, wife's death feed into local legend of "cursed" mansion
item.description: When Mike Harding, a California transplant, spotted a majestic mansion in Celina, Tennessee, he thought he'd found the dream retirement home for himself and his wife, Julie. But those dreams ended abruptly when Mike suddenly went missing in 2022.

item.title: The Mansion Above Dale Hollow Lake
item.description: After a man is murdered and his wife is found dead, it feeds into a local legend of a "cursed" house. "48 Hours" correspondent Peter Van Sant reports.

item.title: At least 12 injured, including 6 children, in Tallahassee shooting
item.description: Police say a fight broke out prior to the shooting.

item.title: Security cameras upend man's story of finding wife fatally shot in his car
item.description: David Tolbert told investigators when he opened his car door outside a store where he was working in Huntsville, Alabama, he discovered his wife Savannah Tolbert's lifeless body in the front passenger seat. Investigators would rely on multiple security cameras to piece together what happened.

item.title: What the Cameras Saw
item.description: Multiple surveillance cameras capture the final moments of what happened before a mysterious figure ends a woman's life. "48 Hours" correspondent Anne-Marie Green reports.

item.title: In the Venezuelan stronghold of Doral, some voters discouraged by Trump's policies
item.description: Doral, Florida, has the largest Venezuelan population of any city in the country.

item.title: New memorial honors Gulf War veterans
item.description: A new memorial honors veterans of the Gulf War who liberated Kuwait from Saddam Hussein. Eleanor Watson has the story.

item.title: More than 1,000 arrested in France as protesters and police clash
item.description: While demonstrations throughout France were largely peaceful, police reported clashes with protesters Saturday evening.

item.title: 1 arrested after fire at Hitler's Eagle's Nest mountain retreat
item.description: Police said firefighting efforts were hampered due to local conditions.

item.title: German police arrest suspect following fire at Hitler's Eagle's Nest
item.description: German police said they have arrested a 33-year-old suspect following a fire at an alpine retreat known as Eagle's Nest that was once used by the Nazis and Adolf Hitler.

item.title: DOJ demands that some California counties set aside alleged noncitizen ballots
item.description: Federal prosecutors sent letters to county registrars across California demanding that local officials set aside and verify ballots that the Justice Department said may belong to noncitizens.

item.title: In one Miami community, some Latinos hesitant to vote Republican amid ICE immigration crackdown
item.description: In Doral, Florida, some Latino voters who had previously been supportive of President Trump are turning away from the Republican Party amid strong activity from U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Cristian Benavides reports.

item.title: New York City votes to ban horse-drawn carriages
item.description: The New York City Council voted Thursday to ban horse-drawn carriages by 2028 over safety and animal abuse concerns. Ali Bauman has more.

item.title: France see new round of protests; Riot police clash with demonstrators in Italy
item.description: More anti-government protests took place in France this weekend. Leigh Kiniry has the details.

item.title: SpaceX satellite system back up to full speed in Ukraine, officials say
item.description: Ukrainian leaders confirmed Saturday that the country's access to SpaceX technologies Starlink and Starshield have been restored to full speed, shortly after Elon Musk admitted to slowing Starlink down.

item.title: Obama hits the campaign trail for Democrats with midterms less than 2 weeks away
item.description: Former President Barack Obama was hitting multiple campaign stops in Ohio and Michigan this weekend to speak out against the Trump administration, with midterms less than two weeks away. Nikole Killion has more.

item.title: West Coast communities bracing for high tides as storms bring flooding
item.description: Communities along the West Coast were bracing for high tides to add to recent flooding that has also inundated the Southwest. Akiko Fujita reports, and Andrew Kozak has the forecast.

item.title: In Ohio rally, Obama blasts Ramaswamy, GOP over controversial Acton ad
item.description: Former President Barack Obama took aim at gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy, who has doubled down on an advertising campaign featuring the estranged mother of Democratic rival Amy Acton.

item.title: 10/24: CBS Weekend News
item.description: West Coast braces for more flooding; Obama campaigns for Democrats.

item.title: Elon Musk says SpaceX throttled Ukraine Starlink speeds over drone strikes
item.description: SpaceX's military-grade version of the Starlink internet service has become the backbone of Ukraine's drone operations.

item.title: The controversy surrounding convicted former election official Tina Peters
item.description: President Trump has gone to extraordinary lengths for Tina Peters, a former Colorado election official convicted for helping to breach the very voting system she swore to protect. Peters served less than two years in prison for crimes related to breaching voting system security. She maintains she was trying to show flaws in the system. 60 Minutes reports, Sunday.

item.title: 60 Minutes investigates "third-country deportations"
item.description: As the Trump administration seeks to carry out the largest deportation in American history, it is removing more and more people to countries they are not from and often have no ties to. It's called "third-country deportation." A 60 Minutes investigation reveals how some of these third countries are forcing deportees back to the nations they fled, places where U.S. immigration judges have ruled they could not be sent because they'd likely face persecution or torture.

item.title: 2 ex-FBI officials charged with lying about Hunter Biden laptop probe
item.description: Two former FBI agents have each been charged with one count of lying to Congress about the investigation into Hunter Biden's laptop.

item.title: Medicare Advantage plans cut for 1 million seniors, insurers say
item.description: Two of the largest private insurers are discontinuing some Medicare Advantage plans amid higher costs and a spike in utilization.

item.title: AI agents detected inside customer bank accounts, report says
item.description: Banks have detected personal AI agent activity inside customers' accounts as experts warn about the risks of oversharing with AI.

item.title: Inside Australia's social media ban for children | Sunday on 60 Minutes
item.description: Last year, Australia became the first country in the world to force many social media companies to prevent children from having accounts. There are high stakes for children as well as big tech's bottom line. Holly Williams reports Sunday on 60 Minutes.

item.title: More people now use GLP-1s to lose weight than for other health issues
item.description: Growing usage of GLP-1 drugs for weight loss is reshaping how consumers shop for food and clothes, according to consulting firm EY-Parthenon.
